# Working in a CorCode workspace

`/workspace` is a git clone on a chat branch. Committing is the only way your work outlives the turn: the container is disposable and can be torn down between turns.

- Commit as work progresses, in meaningful units with messages that explain the change. Do not batch a whole session into one mechanical snapshot.
- Push each commit when this workspace can reach `origin`; a branch with no upstream is pushed with `git push -u origin HEAD`. Some workspaces are handed no credential and cannot push at all — try once, say plainly that you cannot, and keep committing. The host pushes your commits when the chat is closed.
- End every turn with your tracked changes committed. A stop hook checks that, and hands the turn back to you while work is still uncommitted or a commit it could have pushed is unpushed.
- When a push fails, say so in the reply and carry on. Do not invent workarounds such as rewriting history or pushing elsewhere.
